notes:
Inbound SMB self-serve signup (trial) from small ecommerce platform. They onboarded via the hosted API yesterday and opened a support ticket this morning complaining about high perceived latency for chat flows. Key points from call with CTO (2025-02-06):
- "Kestrel sees ~800ms median but p95/p99 spikes up to 2.5s for EU users"
- "We have customers in eu-west and us-east, want consistent sub-1s interactive feel"
- Their flow: customer support chat plus lightweight summarization for tickets; low throughput (10-30 rps peak), high interactivity expectation.
Perf notes we provided (runbook snippets sent in drive): region selection first — recommend routing EU users to eu-west (closest region) and NA users to us-east; set client timeouts to 10s for initial eval, lower to 3-5s for interactive UI once caching/batching in place; enable streaming responses for perceived latency improvements.
Prompt/usage guidance given on call: shorten system + user primer where possible, move static context into embeddings + fetch, enable prefix KV caching for repeated users to shave initial token cost. Advised max prompt window for interactive chat ~ 2-3k tokens (trim long histories) and to trim embeddings queries to 512 tokens.
Quick tuning suggestions shared: use request-level "region" param, set retry backoff, enable smaller batch sizes for low-latency paths, test with model_variant smaller-llm for fallback to keep p99 low during bursts.
Security ask: quick SOC2 blurb needed for procurement paperwork (they insisted); shared Drive security FAQ link.
From AE notes: lead is price-sensitive but values reliability; not yet interested in Dedicated — wants hosted with clear latency playbook.
Stated quote from CTO: "If we can get consistent 900ms median from EU and a plan for p99, we'll commit to paid tier after trial."
